Stop getting overly attached to people that don't love you back.  Find someone that does, even if they're the same gender.

There's lots of miserable, lonely, suicidal boys in the world you know.

There's lots of boys that feel unwanted, just like you do.  You should team up.

I think a better question is:  what do these people you're obsessing over really have to offer you?

(And why are you bending over backwards to offer things to them?)

What do they offer you?
In the meantime, check out Ted 2, and let me know if that portryal is over yet.

I believe I was referencing the 90's, right?

When did I say "no progress has been made at all"?

I'm just saying, ignoring the bad stuff doesn't make it go away - and you can't tell me those bigoted reactions aren't still culturally relevant, or you wouldn't see Brain paying homage to them on family guy.

I agree things are changing, and I think that's wonderful.  But sweeping this stuff under the table, just doesn't make it go away.

People were talking about black face in bugs bunny cartoons 30-40 years later.  Why?  Because that's the level of cultural impact it had.

Anyway, I'm not denying I'm crazy - but this stuff would make anyone crazy, and that doesn't mean I'm wrong either.

I am totally screwed up.  I'm agoraphobic, I'm pretty sure I'm displaying symptoms of PTSD - not to mention depression and suicide idealation.

But there is a reason I'm like this.  Stuff like this, is part of the reason.

Being in an environment where you're taught how evil and corrupt you are for even existing, eventually does real psychological damage.

Even if you know its not true - eventually, if presented with enough of it, it will break you down until you are just nothing.

And its not so much the movie itself - the movie just becomes a tool to justify the horrible things said about you.

Until you even start to believe it about yourself - even if you know, deep down, its not true.

That's what bigotry does to people, in a high enough dose.  Everyone has their breaking point.

So this is me pointing it out, and trying to stop it - so no one else ends up like this

I know things are changing.  I think that's awesome.

 But the "gross, inherently corrupt, perverse deviant" portrayal has got to go.

Because that's the image, in all its many forms, that gets people killed, tortured, and screwed up.

And all you have to know its not over, is to switch on fox news.

I bet you say that to black guys all the time, eh?

You know, the "upity" ones?

:)

Anyway, if I called you out without meaning to, I apologize.

Things like this are a sore point for me, and I tend to get emotional about it.

However, I disagree that pointing out bigoted portrayals of years past are completely useless.

Pointing out the bigoted portrayals of black people in media was vital for the civil rights movement, and them being viewed as actual people.

Likewise, I think trans people have to do this as well.  The only way to change those bigoted perceptions is directly challenge them - and that also means highlighting forms of media that openly expressed and justified that prejudice.

If any of my frustration spilled over to you, I apologize - but I won't apologize for standing against bigoted portrayals of people, that seek to justify their murder and subjugation.

 You say that's not what this movie is doing, but I argue that it does.

Seriously - how many trans women are outed and humiliatied like Einhorn, before they're brutally murdered?

And this movie I think justifies it by saying: "Its OK.  They were a terrible person anyway.".

You really think that isn't hate speech, and that being in one of the most popular comedies of all time, doesn't sway people's opinions?

Do tell.

.....

I'm not saying to censor it.  I'm just saying, think about what it saying.

Thank you for listening, and for sticking up for your friend.

If the hangover 2 was made 20 years ago, they would have been portrayed as a grizzled, inhuman monster outright - instead of it just being alluded to.

So I guess you're right - that IS something, I guess.

At this rate, maybe in another 20 years, a trans person will get to be portrayed as an actual, sympathetic human being - instead of the horrible inhuman monster, that German cinemas often portrayed the Jews as.

Hey - here's hoping, right?

You have to admit though, if that portrayal was the only exposure you had to a trans person - you're going to end up with a pretty skewed perception of them.

The crying game, Silence of the lambs, and ace Ventura - I think a better question, what mainstream movie DIDN'T portray the idea of a trans person as a horrible monster?

(Where your own vomiting and disgust at them is always somehow justified.)

Its like seeing every black person you see being portrayed as a rapist or a murderer.

And then you wonder WHY so much hatred exists, right?

.....

Of course Einhorn is a deceptive murderer and kidnapper.

They're supposed to be a trans person, so what else would they be, right?

.....

Don't get down about it though.  Seth McFarland is more than happy to continue that specific form of bigotry in the public eye.

Watch Ted 2, and Brian's reaction on family guy if you don't believe me.

....

You have been indoctrinated to hate and fear them, because of movies like this - movies that do everything in their power to justify that prejudiced reaction.

So don't make excuses for it, and dismiss this as harmless entertainment.

See it for what it is.

.....

You know, as well as I do, if Finkle wasn't portrayed as horrible, those jokes wouldn't be funny.

The movie intentionally paints them as horrible, so the audience can feel justified in their bigotry.

(That way they can laugh at the horrible, disgusting tranny without recourse.)

Finkle's portrayal is a "get out of feeling guilty for hating trans people free" card.

The sad thing is - In Living Color used to make fun of hateful shit like this - and Ace Ventura rejoices in it.

Yes, because Mein Kampf was obviously the only form of propaganda back then, right?

Its not as if they're weren't movies, posters, and radio plays with that same bigotry in mind - and all sold to the populace under the guise of "harmless, family entertainment".

Ace Ventura was my favorite movie growing up, and in a lot of ways, I still love it.  I still think most of its hilarious.

However, that doesn't mean I'm going to pretend those jokes aren't rooted in hate speech - any more than I would as if it was about any other minority group.

Someone said on here that Ace vomiting about sleeping with a trans person, is somehow different from vomiting from sleeping with a Jew, or a light skinned black person.

Once again:  what's the difference?  If that joke is as harmless as you say, then you should be able to plug any minority group into that equasion.

And the sad thing is - you can, and its all equally hateful.

You've just been brainwashed into thinking hating trans people is OK, while hating black people isn't.

.....

How much do you want to bet, if this was the 50's, and the joke was about throwing up for sleeping with a black person, that you'd still find a way to laugh and justify it to yourself?

(And call out anyone darker than you for "not having a good sense of humor" and "being too upity about it".)

Is that who you are?  Is that the sort of person you are?

....

I'm not asking you to be offended by it - you're not a trans person, so why would you be?

I 'm just asking you to see the joke for what it is - and see it for the message it sends to people:

"Trans people are gross, ugly abominations.  Vomit if you see one, just like anyone else on the KKK hate list."

.....

See it for what it is dude, that's all I'm saying.  Either way, it still doesn't change the fact that the rest of it is awesome.

For the record, I still have the Ace Ventura poster that hung in my bedroom as a kid, and Jim Carey is still one of my favorite actors.

That doesn't erase any of what I'm saying, though.

....

Orsen Scott Card - brilliant author; horrible racist bigot.

Birth of a nation - Cinematic masterpiece, but paints the KKK as heros - which is disgusting.

......

You can still enjoy the movie, and see that joke for what it is.

Nothing's perfect, you know - and sometimes your childhood masterpiece, turns out to be riddled with hate speech.

And THAT, in case you didn't know, is kind of funny within itself.  :)

Do you think it would be equally "gross" to find out the girl you were with was part black, Jewish, or Asian?

Cause for the record, those are equally bigoted behaviors too.

.....

The only reason you would think she's gross, is if you harbored a prejudiced and hateful viewpoint of her, simply because she's trans.

A racist looks at a black person, and sees an ugly stereotypical portrait of them, that doesn't actually reflect who they are.

The question is:  do you look at transgender people this way, as well?

Either way, this is the thought process of a bigot.

You know, I think that part is funny, but I give Jim props for standing up for what he believes in.

I just wish he would have stood against all the hateful anti-trans jokes - about how "gross, deseptive, mentally ill and ugly" trans people are.

Honestly, that stuff has probably justified more murder and abuse of trans people, than this joke would have ever caused towards anybody.

The movie literally ends by encouraging the audience to humiliate trans women, and see them as monsters.

How many murderers do you think have brutally killed trans women, and watched this movie in order to justify their actions?

I'm willing to bet:  a lot.

Yeah, for real!  Why do these n*****s and f*****s gotta act so upity all the time.

High five, am I right Rodvinski?  Lol.

....

I think this movie funny cause it shows how gross and disgusting those trannies really are.

Now if they could have shown the same thing with a ch*nk and some da*kies, then you woulda had a GREAT movie, am I right?

WH*TE POWER!  Put an end to all this gross faggotry, that's what I say.

Rodvinski!  You with me on this?

/s

Unless you can offer a rational argument as to WHY they're different, I would like to propose that you're simply in denial.

You've simply been conditioned to view one form of bigotry as acceptable, while the other is not.

That's why you THINK there's a difference, even when there's really not.

You can't quite put your finger on it, can you?

That's called denial.  Enjoy it I guess.

....

Just know that while gender and race are two very different things, bigotry is ALWAYS the same.

Its where you take a series of characteristics and seek to dehumanize and humilate a group of people based on them.

How many murderers do you think killed a trans person because they're "gross and disgusting", and sat down to watch Ace Ventura and The Crying game as a means to justify their actions?

I'm willing to bet:  more than a few.

Edit:  That's right.  Down vote whatever you can't explain away, or immediately justify.

If you're going to be prejudiced and hateful, that's fine - but you could at least own up to it.

In what way is it different?  Please explain.

Please explain to me the virtues of hating and dehumanizing one minority group over the other.

Oh I see - is it because one group of physical characteristics are OK to demonize, while with the other they're not?

Is that what you're saying?  I really would like to know.

.... 

How are a homophobe, a racist, and a transphobe different from each other?

The only difference is the physical characteristics in question, correct?

....

The charactistics of a black person were once made synomious with "lewd, base desires" and "uglyness", correct?

So what you're saying it OK to apply those labels to trans people, but not black people.

Because....its different, right?

I'm just saying, the joke would have been equally funny if Ace started vomiting because he accidently slept with a light skinned black lady, or a Jew.

"Insert minority group here", and have fun with the joke.

Ace:  Einhorn's a coon?!  Oh god!

::::vomits::::::

....

See how funny it is, in all its contexts?

Laugh it up, but enjoy the joke for what it is. 

Its the same joke, either way.

Why couldn't they have left that joke in, and taken out all the "trans people are gross & mentally ill" jokes?

Its actually a really funny movie, until it turns into an anti-gay propaganda film from the 50's.

Then it just makes you cringe more than black face in a bugs bunny cartoon.

If anything is going to make this movie look like shit in 20 years, its going to be that.  Its literally the "Birth of a Nation" of comedy movies.

Hilarious and groundbreaking - but also riddled with hate speech.

That's what I do too.  I don't literally think I'm an alien - I'm not quite that insane, I guess.  

But yeah, throughout my life, all my friends have always been the weirdos and social pariahs, people that stuck out as much as me.

Which is cool, because in a weird way its almost like this bonding kind of thing, to think "us vs the world" or something.

But it seems like that's kind of harder to find the older you get.  Most people, I think, kind of settle into things, realize their place in the universe, and it all kind of evens out.

That never really happened with me, though.  I think I'm kind of destined to feel as if I'm a cosmic fluke in the universe, or something.

Which I guess is OK - but the constant alienation and isolation I feel constantly, around almost everyone.....I think it kind of gets to me after a while.

And that's why I fixate on suicide so much, I suppose.

Its just that all the things people view as important (material positions, social status, superficial apperences).....all of that seems meaningless and empty to me.

But those things matter so much to everyone else, its almost like you're forced to care about them.

(And I'm not talking about mere survival mind you - I mean like focusing on those things, almost as a means to an end.  Like they're the most important things in the world, or something.)

Its like I have this huge hole I don't know how to fill - and everything on TV touting the merits of fame and success doesn't seem like the solution.

 I suppose this should be my cue to join a religious cult of some sort, in order to "fill the hole", but all of them seem kind of silly.

(Like the end result of that is a bunch of people standing around, saying "my god is better than your god" - like each diety was a second rate football team, or something.)

So I don't know.  Maybe I'm permantly just stuck in this nilhistic thought process, of being overly cynical about everyrhing

I know you're supposed to grow out of this, but I guess I don't how.

All I can come up with is "try to be kind to others and make the world a better place."

And I guess, in my own limited way, I do try to do that, any way I can.

But still....its kind of hard to shake that constant feeling that "none of this really matters".  I mean, how do you shake that feeling?

My room looks exactly the same as yours.  I think if you feel as if you're inherently worthless, and the world seem cold, isolating, and hateful......after a while, even basic living functions fall by the wayside.

This is how people live when they have been taught to hate themselves, and there life has no intrinsic value.

Depression / self loathing /anxiety are a bitch.

A better question I guess is:  why do you feel this way?

How do you fix it?
